title: Differential rank at points of fibres of a smooth polynomial quotient
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $n,c\geq0$, $f_1,\ldots,f_c\in R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], $J=(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$ and $Q=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/J$. Assume $Q$ is smooth over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] and $J/J^2$ has a $Q$-basis indexed by $\{1,\ldots,c\}$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Let $\mathfrak p$ be a prime of $R$, $T=\kappa(\mathfrak p)\otimes_R Q$ and $\mathfrak q$ a prime of $T$, with $K=\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Then $c\leq n$ and $\dim_K(K\otimes_T\Omega_{T/\kappa(\mathfrak p)})=n-c$, where differentials are [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] and dimension is [def-weil-vector-space-dimension]. The chosen basis need not be the equation classes.

source.place: Lemma Tag 07CG (lemma-syntomic-complete-intersection), fibre-dimension sentence; Lemma Tag 07CH (lemma-smooth-standard-smooth), split conormal sequence in the opening of the proof. Read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07CG and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07CH.

proof.text: Put J=(f_1,...,f_c), Q=R[x_1,...,x_n]/J. The polynomial generators and the given equations give a finite presentation of Q [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]; its extension cotangent module identifies with J/J², including its Q-module action. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-presentation-localized-conormal-split] at a=1, and identify Q_1 with Q. Localizing at a unit is an isomorphism, so the tensor-localized conormal module is J/J² and the differentials are Ω[Q/R]. Obtain (J/J²) × Ω[Q/R] ≅ Q^n.

Let p be a prime of R, T=κ(p) tensor_R Q, q a prime of T and K=κ(q). Tensor the equivalence of step 1 with K over Q. Tensor products commute with finite products, and the given basis of J/J² base-changes to a basis of cardinality c over K. The coordinate basis of Q^n similarly gives cardinality n. Thus (K tensor_Q J/J²) × (K tensor_Q Ω[Q/R]) ≅ K^n. This is scalar extension of an equivalence, not an appeal to flatness of K.

Differential base change [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-base-change] gives Ω[T/κ(p)] ≅ T tensor_Q Ω[Q/R]. Tensor associativity and cancellation give K tensor_T Ω[T/κ(p)] ≅ K tensor_Q Ω[Q/R]. No conormal flat base-change assertion is used.

The right side K^n is finite-dimensional, hence so are the two summands. The dimension formula for a product and invariance under linear equivalence give c + dim_K(K tensor_T Ω[T/κ(p)]) = n. Natural-number arithmetic yields c ≤ n and dimension n-c. If T=0, there is no q and the assertion has no instance to check.

from.place: Steps 4 and 5 of lem-weil-pbc-smooth-retract-relative-global-complete-intersection: the split conormal sequence and differential base change give rank n-c at a point of a fibre.

lean.statement:
theorem smooth_quotient_fibre_differential_rank
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {n c : ℕ} (f : Fin c → MvPolynomial (Fin n) R)
    [Smooth R (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range f))]
    (b : Module.Basis (Fin c)
      (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range f))
      (Ideal.span (Set.range f)).Cotangent)
    (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime]
    (q : PrimeSpectrum (p.Fiber (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range f)))) :
    c ≤ n ∧ Module.finrank q.asIdeal.ResidueField
      (q.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[p.Fiber
        (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range f))]
          KaehlerDifferential p.ResidueField
            (p.Fiber (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range f)))) = n - c
